source: src/components/operations/OperationsLedger.tsx (DIMENSIONS constant, all 6, D1 Regulatory feasibility through D6 Operational cost data, ~line 84; SOURCED_DIMENSIONS = DIMENSIONS.filter(d => d.key !== 'regulatory') at line 93; passed to RegionDimensionMatrix's `dimensions` prop at line 346) and its own `dek` prop text ('Six dimensions per region · every fact carries a source and date'); 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' p8 (#p8) Dimension filter facet, which lists all six (D1 Regulatory feasibility, D2 Regional resource, D3 Labor markets, D4 Materials sourcing, D5 Infrastructure, D6 Operational cost); operator ruling 3.3 ('Operations matrix renders 5 of 6 dimensions; add D6 Regulatory Feasibility. Six dimensions, D1-D6, same order everywhere.')
notes: CONFIRMED this session by reading OperationsLedger.tsx directly, independent of the ruling: DIMENSIONS defines all 6 in the exact order the p8 filter facet uses; SOURCED_DIMENSIONS immediately filters out the 'regulatory' entry with the comment 'the ones with rows in regional_data_facts', and only SOURCED_DIMENSIONS reaches RegionDimensionMatrix. This is a hardcoded exclusion in OperationsLedger.tsx, not a data-driven gap — the matrix component itself (RegionDimensionMatrix.tsx) takes whatever `dimensions` array it is given and has no 6-vs-5 logic of its own, confirmed by this mount successfully rendering 5 rows for the 5-item array it is fed.

OperationsLedger.tsx's own `dek` prop passed to ListSurfaceShell literally reads 'Six dimensions per region' while the matrix beneath it renders five — a self-contradiction inside the product's own copy, independent of any design-source comparison.

This mount reproduces OperationsLedger.tsx's DIMENSIONS/SOURCED_DIMENSIONS constants verbatim (copied into mounts.mjs, not re-derived), so the row count measured here is the same 5 a real page render produces.

This spec's fix point is named for the record only — this lane writes no product code (audit harness lane, uxaudit-c): OperationsLedger.tsx:93's filter is the single line ruling 3.3 requires a fix lane to remove.
